claims.claim: The serpent shadow effect appears for several weeks around the equinoxes, not just on one day
claims.quote: it has been shown that the phenomenon can be observed, without major changes, during several weeks around the equinoxes, making it impossible to determine any date by observing this effect alone.

claims.claim: The effect occurs in the late afternoon around both the spring and autumn equinoxes, when the northwest corner casts triangular shadows on the western balustrade of the north stairway
claims.quote: Around the Spring and Autumn equinoxes, in the late afternoon, the northwest corner of the pyramid casts a series of triangular shadows against the western balustrade on the north side that evokes the appearance of a serpent wriggling down the staircase

claims.claim: The equinoxshadow.jpg photograph was taken at Chichen Itza during the March 2009 equinox by ATSZ56
claims.quote:
Description: Kukulkan at its finest during the March Equinox. Chichen Itza Equinox March 2009. The famous descent of the snake at the temple.
Date: 2009-03-21
Author: ATSZ56

claims.claim: In 1892 the Castillo was a bush-covered mound, as shown in Maler's photograph
claims.quote: Chichen Itza, Yucatan, Mexico. Castillo, photograph by Teobert Maler (1842-1917)

claims.claim: Teobert Maler photographed the Castillo in 1892
claims.quote:
Date: 1892
Author: Teoberto Maler

claims.claim: The Mexican government excavated and restored El Castillo (and the Great Ball Court)
claims.quote: At the same time, the Mexican government excavated and restored El Castillo (Temple of Kukulcán) and the Great Ball Court.

claims.claim: The excavation/restoration of El Castillo took place during the 1920s and 1930s
claims.quote: In the mid-1930s, the Mexican government sponsored an excavation of the temple.

claims.claim: Many of the stone buildings at Chichen Itza were originally painted red, green, blue and purple
claims.quote: Many of these stone buildings were originally painted in red, green, blue and purple colors.

claims.claim: Carved serpent heads sit at the base of the balustrades of El Castillo's northeastern staircase
claims.quote: At the base of the balustrades of the northeastern staircase are carved heads of a serpent.

claims.claim: The feathered serpent sculpture is limestone, from Chichén Itzá, dated 900–1250 CE, photographed by Jebulon (CC0)
claims.quote: Feathered snake, ancient post-classic era, 900 - 1250 CE, limestone. From Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico.

claims.claim: The Carnegie Institution's first Chichen Itza staff comprised five people, photographed May 1924
claims.quote: First Staff of the Carnegie Institution of Washington, Chichen Itza Project. From left to right: J.O. Kilmartin, engineer, U.S. Geological Survey; Monroe Amsden, assistant archeologist and paymaster; E.H. Morris, archeologist in charge of excavations, Ann Axtell Morris, artist, and S.G. Morley, Associate of the Institution in charge of the Chichen Itza Project. May 21, 1924.

claims.claim: Five people are visible in the carnegiestaff.jpg photograph, seated under a thatched structure
claims.quote: First Staff of the Carnegie Institution of Washington, Chichen Itza Project. From left to right: J.O. Kilmartin ... S.G. Morley

claims.claim: The staff group included an engineer, a paymaster, an archeologist, an artist and Morley
claims.quote: J.O. Kilmartin, engineer, U.S. Geological Survey; Monroe Amsden, assistant archeologist and paymaster; E.H. Morris, archeologist in charge of excavations, Ann Axtell Morris, artist, and S.G. Morley

claims.claim: The Carnegie Institution received a ten-year excavation permit in 1923
claims.quote: In 1923, the Mexican government awarded the Carnegie Institution a ten-year permit (later extended by another ten years) to allow U.S. archeologists to conduct extensive excavation and restoration of Chichen Itza.

claims.claim: In 2015 scientists determined there is a cenote hidden under the Temple of Kukulcán, never seen by archeologists
claims.quote: In 2015, scientists determined that there is a hidden cenote under the Temple of Kukulkan, which has never been seen by archeologists.

claims.claim: The belief that the shadow effect was designed to record the equinoxes is considered highly unlikely
claims.quote: It is a widespread belief that this light-and-shadow effect was achieved on purpose to record the equinoxes, but the idea is highly unlikely

claims.claim: The pyramid is 30 m high with nine terraces and a 6 m temple on top
claims.quote: This step pyramid stands about 30 meters (98 ft) high and consists of a series of nine square terraces, each approximately 2.57 meters (8.4 ft) high, with a 6-meter (20 ft) high temple upon the summit.

claims.claim: The sides are 55.3 m at the base and the faces rise at 53°
claims.quote: The sides of the pyramid are approximately 55.3 meters (181 ft) at the base and rise at an angle of 53°, although that varies slightly for each side.

claims.claim: Digging in the 1930s found an older temple inside, containing a Chac Mool and a jaguar throne painted red with inlaid jade
claims.quote: Inside the temple chamber was a Chac Mool statue and a throne in the shape of Jaguar, painted red and with spots made of inlaid jade.

claims.claim: 3D scanning in 2025 confirmed an enclosed earlier pyramid, "Castillo-sub", built in successive enlargements
claims.quote: Recent 3D modeling and multimodal scanning in 2025 has revealed an earlier pyramid substructure, deemed "Castillo-sub", that is enclosed within the larger "El Castillo" pyramid structure.

claims.claim: Carnegie's first staff arrived in May 1924
claims.quote: S.G. Morley, Associate of the Institution in charge of the Chichen Itza Project. May 21, 1924.
